questions.question: If your turn signals fail, what should you use to show that you are turning?
questions.correctAnswerText: Hand signals
questions.explanation: If your turn signals do not work, use hand signals to show when you are turning.

questions.question: When a traffic light shows a green arrow with a red light, what does this mean?

options.text: You may only drive straight ahead.
You may drive only in the direction of the green arrow.
You must wait for a solid green light to proceed in any direction.
Vehicles moving in any direction must stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may drive only in the direction of the green arrow.
questions.explanation: A green arrow with a red light means you can only drive in the direction shown by the arrow, and only if the intersection is clear.

questions.question: What shape is a stop sign?
questions.correctAnswerText: Octagon
questions.explanation: Stop signs are eight-sided. All eight-sided signs tell drivers to come to a complete stop.

questions.question: Under Alaska law, who must use seat belts?

options.text: Only people in the front seat
Everyone in a moving vehicle at all times
Only when driving faster than 50 mph

questions.correctAnswerText: Everyone in a moving vehicle at all times
questions.explanation: Everyone in a vehicle must wear a seat belt. The driver is responsible for making sure all passengers under 16 use seat belts.

questions.question: Why should you use extra caution near a pedestrian with a white cane?
questions.correctAnswerText: They are blind
questions.explanation: A white cane means the person is blind. Slow down, give them the right-of-way, and be ready to stop.

questions.question: What can help prevent rear-end collisions?

options.text: Check your mirrors and blind spots before stopping
Release the gas pedal to slow down before using the brakes

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above
questions.explanation: Avoid sudden stops. Check mirrors and blind spots before stopping. Release the gas pedal to slow down gradually, then apply steady brake pressure.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The right lane ends and traffic must merge left

questions.correctAnswerText: The right lane ends and traffic must merge left
questions.explanation: This sign shows that the right lane is ending. Traffic in that lane must move to the left.

questions.question: What should you do at a flashing red traffic light?

options.text: Proceed only when it is safe
Treat it like a stop sign

questions.correctAnswerText: All of these
questions.explanation: Treat a flashing red light like a stop sign. Come to a complete stop, look both ways for traffic and pedestrians, then proceed only when it is safe.

questions.question: Your tire blows out while driving. What should you do?

options.text: Hold the steering wheel firmly and slow to a stop
Turn on flashers and continue driving

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the steering wheel firmly and slow to a stop
questions.explanation: Do not slam on the brakes. Grip the wheel firmly and stay in your lane. Release the gas pedal to slow down gradually, then apply light brake pressure and move to a safe area.

questions.question: What should you do before changing lanes on a multilane road?

options.text: Honk your horn to alert drivers behind you
Slow down to reduce your blind spot
Check mirrors, then look straight ahead

questions.correctAnswerText: None of these
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors and look over your shoulder to check your blind spot before changing lanes.

questions.question: An octagonal sign is always a:
questions.correctAnswerText: Stop sign.
questions.explanation: Octagonal signs are always stop signs. You must come to a complete stop when you see a red, eight-sided sign.

questions.question: You turn onto a two-lane road with a broken yellow line down the middle. This means:

options.text: You are on a two-way road.
You are on a one-way road.
You must stay to the left of the broken yellow lines.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are on a two-way road.
questions.explanation: Yellow centerlines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. A broken yellow line means you may cross it to pass slower traffic when it is safe.

questions.question: You are on a two-lane road with no bicycle lane and see a cyclist ahead going the same way. What is the safest way to pass?

options.text: Slow down and wait for no oncoming traffic, then pass while giving the cyclist plenty of space.
Keep driving straight. The cyclist must get out of your way.
Do not pass until you reach a traffic light or stop sign.
Honk to let the cyclist know you are about to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and wait for no oncoming traffic, then pass while giving the cyclist plenty of space.
questions.explanation: Pass a cyclist like you would pass any other vehicle. Keep at least 3 feet of space between your mirror and the cyclist. On higher speed roads or when passing multiple cyclists, leave at least 5 feet. Do not honk unless necessary, as it may startle the rider.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Two-way traffic.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings. They tell you about road conditions and hazards ahead. This sign warns you that traffic may be coming from the opposite direction.

questions.question: When driving across railroad tracks that have no signals or gates:

options.text: You have the right-of-way and do not need to check for trains.
You may pass slower drivers while crossing the tracks.
Make sure your vehicle can cross completely without stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure your vehicle can cross completely without stopping.
questions.explanation: Before driving onto railroad tracks, check that you have enough space to cross completely. Never pass another vehicle at a railroad crossing. Always look for trains before crossing any tracks.

questions.question: When driving past a car that just parked on the roadside, you should:

options.text: Assume the driver will open the car door as you approach.
Assume the driver will wait for you to pass before opening the door.

questions.correctAnswerText: Assume the driver will open the car door as you approach.
questions.explanation: Assume a parked car's door may open as you pass. Be extra careful when driving near parked vehicles.

questions.question: Two solid yellow lines mean:

options.text: Passing is allowed from both directions.
Passing is allowed at the top of a hill.
Passing is allowed during daylight only.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing is not allowed.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. Never cross two solid yellow lines to pass from either direction.

questions.question: If your car breaks down on a highway, you should:

options.text: Stay in your car and wait for help.
Turn on your four-way flashers to warn other drivers.
Flash your headlights at oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your four-way flashers to warn other drivers.
questions.explanation: Turn on your hazard flashers and carefully exit the road. Park as far off the road as possible where other drivers can see you. Lift your hood to show that your vehicle has broken down.

questions.question: On slippery roads, you should:

options.text: Drive the speed limit with caution.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: Slow down when rain, snow, or sleet makes the road slippery. Safety may require driving slower than the posted speed limit when road conditions are poor.

questions.question: What does a single dashed yellow line separating traffic mean?

options.text: Drivers may pass if it is safe to do so.
Both lanes travel in the same direction.
Drivers may pass, even if it could be dangerous.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers may pass if it is safe to do so.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. A single dashed yellow line means drivers in both directions may pass if it is safe. Only pass if you will not interfere with oncoming traffic.
